text.p01: To everyone who has ever fallen down: you can always get up again. In Japan there is an old saying: nana korobi ya oki, "fall down seven times, get up eight." Little roly-poly dolls that always pop back up have carried that saying for hundreds of years. Falling is how we learn. Getting up is up to us.
text.p03: High in the snowy mountains lived Yuki, a little mountain goat with fluffy gray fur and a white star on her forehead.
text.p04: Every morning, the big goats leaped up to Cloud Rock to watch the sunrise. "One day," said Yuki, "I'll climb up there too."
text.p05: Her best friend was Taro, a snow monkey who loved warm springs and his little red roly-poly toy.
text.p06: Whenever it tipped over, it rocked, and rolled, and popped right back up. Wobble, wobble... POP! "It never stays down," said Taro proudly.
text.p07: One snowy day, Yuki began to climb. Hop, hop, hop... onto a shiny rock. Whoosh! Her hooves slipped, and down she tumbled.
text.p08: She landed in a soft pile of snow. The big goats leaped right past her. Yuki's cheeks felt hot. "Maybe I'm just not a climber."
text.p09: Taro tipped over his toy. Wobble, wobble... POP! Yuki looked back at the shiny rock. "Shiny rocks are slippery," she said slowly.
text.p10: So she got up and tried again, stepping on crunchy snow instead. Up she went... until a little stone rolled. Bump! Down again.
text.p11: And again. And again. By sunset, Yuki had fallen four times. She sat in the pink snow, tired and wobbly, and rested for a while.
text.p12: Then she thought about each fall. Shiny rocks slip. Little stones roll. Rushing trips. Big jumps miss. "Every fall taught me something!"
text.p13: Day after day, Yuki practiced. Crunchy snow. Big stones. Slow steps. Small jumps. When she fell, she shook off the snow and got up.
text.p14: Fall number five. Fall number six. Wobble, wobble... POP! Each time she got up, Yuki climbed a little higher than before.
text.p15: One foggy morning, Yuki found Hina, a little snow bird, crying at the bottom of the hill. "I fell," she sniffed. "I can't do it."
text.p16: Yuki sat down beside her. "I've fallen six times," she said. "Falling just teaches you things. Want to know what I learned?" Hina nodded.
text.p17: Before sunrise, Yuki set off for Cloud Rock, with Taro and Hina cheering below. Up and up she climbed, until the top was almost there.
text.p18: Then a gust of wind blew. Whoosh! Yuki slid all the way down the steep, snowy slope. Fall number seven, the biggest of all.
text.p19: Yuki lay in the snow. The top looked so far away now. Then she heard it: wobble, wobble... POP! Taro was holding up his toy.
text.p20: Yuki got up. Crunchy snow. Big stones. Slow steps. Small jumps. And when the wind blew, she leaned in close to the mountain.
text.p21: Step by step, she climbed onto Cloud Rock as the sun came up. Below her, a sea of soft clouds stretched far, far away.
text.p22: "Seven falls," Yuki laughed, "and eight times up!" Then she called down to Hina, "Crunchy snow! Big stones! Slow steps! You can do it too!"
text.p23: By spring, Hina and all the little ones could climb Cloud Rock too. Yuki still fell sometimes. But now she just laughed, and got up.
text.p24: Wobble, wobble... POP! went the little red toy, rolling right back up. Fall seven times, get up eight. The End
text.cover: Eight Times Up. A Story About Falling Down and Getting Up Again
